scheme_name: XLRI – Xavier School of Management Startup Support
overview: XLRI – Xavier School of Management is India's oldest management school, established in 1949 by Jesuit Fathers, dedicated to nurturing responsible global leaders through academic excellence, ethical conduct, and social responsibility. The institution offers a range of residential and online postgraduate diploma programmes in areas such as Business Management, Human Resource Management, Innovation, Entrepreneurship & Venture Development, and Logistics & Supply Chain Management. XLRI emphasizes ethical and socially responsible management education, with a strong focus on innovation, entrepreneurship, and sustainable development through various centres and initiatives.
objectives: Nurture responsible global leaders for the greater common good and a sustainable future
Promote innovation and entrepreneurship through academic programmes and centres like CARA
Develop ethical and socially responsible management education
Support student-driven AI incubator projects in collaboration with AI Clubs
Encourage critical thinking, continuous improvement, and a culture of innovation
Extend frontiers of knowledge through relevant and contextual research
Inculcate a culture of innovation and entrepreneurship
Empower research endeavors and innovative projects addressing real-world business challenges
eligibility: Eligibility varies by programme; for residential PGDM programmes, candidates must appear for XAT (Xavier Aptitude Test) and meet academic criteria as specified in the admissions section. For online programmes, eligibility is based on academic qualifications and work experience as outlined for each programme. Specific eligibility for innovation and entrepreneurship support is not detailed in the evidence.
benefits: Students benefit from a world-class academic environment, experienced faculty, strong industry linkages, placement opportunities, access to centres like CARA for AI research and application, participation in innovation and entrepreneurship activities, exposure to rural immersion programmes, and a robust alumni network. The institute emphasizes holistic development, ethical leadership, and social responsibility, preparing students to address unmet societal needs through innovation and sustainable practices.
financial_support: The evidence does not specify any direct financial support, grants, loans, or funding mechanisms for startups or entrepreneurs under a formal scheme. Financial references in the text pertain to alumni donations, endowment funds, infrastructure costs (e.g., proposed new campus costing Rs. 50–60 crores), and scholarships for students, not startup-specific financial aid.
application_process: 1. Visit the official XLRI admissions page at https://xlri.ac.in/admissions 2. Check eligibility for the desired programme (PGDM, online, or certificate) 3. Register and appear for XAT (for PGDM programmes) or meet direct eligibility (for online programmes) 4. Fill out the online application form 5. Upload required documents including academic transcripts, XAT scorecard, work experience details, and identity proof 6. Pay the application fee 7. Submit the application and await shortlisting for further stages such as group discussion and personal interview 8. Final selection based on cumulative performance.
required_documents: Category certificate (if applying under reserved category)
Statement of purpose or essay (as required by programme)
deadlines: Application deadlines vary by programme and are announced annually on the admissions portal. For XAT-based programmes, deadlines typically align with the XAT exam schedule (usually January). Online and certificate programmes may have rolling or periodic admissions. Specific dates are not provided in the evidence.
contact_details: Email: admissions@xlri.ac.in | Phone: Not explicitly stated in evidence
caveats: Financial support for startups or entrepreneurs is not explicitly detailed in the evidence
No dedicated startup funding scheme or incubation fund is described in the provided pages
Innovation and entrepreneurship support is primarily academic and experiential (e.g., via CARA, student projects, IEV programme) rather than direct financial grants or loans
